    AI Overview
    +3
    Víctor Martínez ("V-Mart") is a retired Venezuelan MLB catcher and designated hitter known for his switch-hitting power and consistent batting with the Indians, Red Sox, and Tigers (2002–2018). A 5-time All-Star, he finished his career with a .295 average and was a key part of Detroit's lineup. 
    Key Career Highlights and Details 
    • Teams: Cleveland Indians (2002–2009), Boston Red Sox (2009–2010), Detroit Tigers (2011–2018).
    • Victor Martinez Contract/Salary: In 2014, he signed a four-year, $68 million contract extension with the Detroit Tigers, cementing his role as a premier designated hitter
      .
    • Victor Martinez Home Runs: He finished his 16-year career with 246 home runs and 1,178 RBI.
    • Achievements: Two-time Silver Slugger Award winner and a 5-time All-Star.
    • Playing Style: Recognized as one of the most reliable switch-hitters of his era, often producing high batting averages and low strikeout totals.
    • Retirement: Retired after the 2018 season. 
    Notes 
    • Note: This information refers to the Major League Baseball player. It is not related to the pro bodybuilder of the same name.

    Víctor Jesús Martínez, also known by his nickname "V-Mart", is a Venezuelan former professional baseball catcher and designated hitter. Martínez played in Major League Baseball for the Cleveland Indians, Boston Red Sox, and Detroit Tigers. After joining the Tigers, he played mostly as a designated hitter.
